analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on dengue virus, specifically examining the identification of non-invasive biomarkers for dengue infection and its progression to severe forms such as dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) and dengue shock syndrome (DSS). The central question is whether metabolomic approaches can provide reliable, non-invasive markers for dengue disease severity.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and searched PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science for studies applying NMR- or MS-based metabolomics to human dengue samples. Eligibility criteria required a healthy-control or severity comparison group, and 17 studies were included after screening.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identified three convergent patterns associated with increasing dengue severity: depletion of serotonin and related tryptophan-pathway metabolites, disturbance of glycerophospholipid and lysophospholipid classes, and elevation of markers of hepatic and lipid-metabolic stress. Serotonin combined with IFN-γ showed the strongest discriminatory performance for progression to DHF, with an AUC of 0.92.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is scattered across biofluids and analytical platforms, with most studies focusing on blood-derived matrices. No eligible study examined alternative biofluids such as feces, saliva, tears, sweat, or cerebrospinal fluid, highlighting a gap in non-invasive biomarker research.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should explore alternative biofluids for non-invasive biomarker development. Additionally, further studies are needed to validate the identified metabolic signatures and their utility in predicting disease severity.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the use of metabolomic approaches to identify non-invasive biomarkers for dengue infection and its progression to severe forms. The review synthesized 17 studies that applied NMR- or MS-based metabolomics to human dengue samples, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Key findings include three consistent metabolic patterns associated with increasing disease severity: depletion of serotonin and tryptophan pathway metabolites, disturbance of phospholipid classes, and elevation of hepatic and lipid stress markers. Serotonin combined with IFN-γ demonstrated the strongest discriminatory performance for predicting progression to DHF. This highlights a need for further research into alternative, more accessible biofluids for non-invasive biomarker development.

abstract_zh: 登革热是一种主要的蚊媒病毒性疾病,其从自限性发热到出血性或休克综合征 (DHF/DSS) 的快速进展仍然难以使用传统的临床标志物进行预测。代谢组学为识别感染和严重程度的非侵入性生物标志物提供了一种有前途的途径,但证据仍然分散在生物体液和分析平台中。本系统综述综合了登革热感染的人类代谢组学研究,以表征迄今为止报道的生物体液、技术和代谢特征。根据 PRISMA 2020 指南,对 PubMed、ScienceDirect 和 Web of Science 进行了搜索,以查找将基于 NMR 或 MS 的代谢组学应用于人类登革热样本的研究,并根据需要健康对照或严重程度对照组的 PECO 标准进行筛选。在确定的 780 项记录中,17 项研究符合所有资格标准。大多数研究 (14/17) 分析了血液基质(血清、血浆或全血),其中三项研究分析了尿液;没有符合条件的研究检查粪便、唾液、眼泪、汗液或脑脊液。研究发现,随着疾病严重程度的增加,出现了三种趋同模式:血清素和相关色氨酸途径代谢物的消耗,甘油磷脂和溶血磷脂类别的紊乱,以及肝脏和脂质代谢应激标志物的升高(胆汁酸、VLDL/LDL变化、酰基肉碱)。血清素与 IFN-γ 联合使用,在 DHF 进展方面取得了最强的判别性能(AUC = 0.92),而尿烷烃和甜菜碱则成为与感染状态和糖尿病等合并症相关的候选非侵入性标志物。这些发现凸显了对血液采样的持续依赖,并且几乎完全缺乏探索替代的、更容易获得的生物流体的研究,这代表了未来登革热非侵入性生物标志物研究的明显差距。

title: 1-Year follow-up evaluation of TAK-003 dengue vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic disease and hospitalisation in adolescents during the 2024–2025 outbreak in São Paulo, Brazil: a test-negative case-control study
abstract: Background Dengue is a growing global health threat. Our initial evaluation of the TAK-003 dengue vaccine in adolescents during the 2024 outbreak in São Paulo State, Brazil, showed short-term protection but suggested possible effectiveness waning after 90-days of the first dose, and had limited power to estimate second-dose effectiveness against hospitalisation. We evaluated 1-year vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic, virologically confirmed dengue and dengue hospitalisation in adolescents during 2024–2025, when DENV-1 and DENV-2 predominated in 2024 followed by increasing DENV-3 transmission in 2025. Methods We did a test-negative case–control study among adolescents aged 10–15 years in São Paulo State between Feb 20, 2024, and Dec 31, 2025. We extracted individual-level information on demographic characteristics, comorbidities, dengue testing, dengue vaccination, hospitalisation, and death during the study period from the national surveillance databases for dengue (SINAN-Dengue; compulsory notification) and the São Paulo State Secretary of Health vaccination registry (Rede Nacional de Dados em Saúde) on Feb 4, 2026. Cases were defined as acute febrile illness episodes with virologically confirmed dengue, as detected by NS1 antigen or RT-PCR testing within 5 days of symptom onset. Controls were test-negative acute febrile illness episodes. Surveillance data were linked to the state vaccination registry. Vaccine effectiveness after one or two TAK-003 doses was estimated with mixed-effects logistic regression. Findings We analysed 166,390 tests: 65,365 from cases and 101,025 from controls. Vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic dengue was 59.2% (95% CI 56.1–62.0) after one dose and 73.1% (69.1–76.6) after two doses. Against dengue hospitalisation, effectiveness was 74.6% (62.7–82.7) after one dose and 87.9% (73.0–94.6) after two doses. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the 1-year effectiveness of the TAK-003 dengue vaccine against symptomatic dengue and hospitalisation in adolescents during the 2024–2025 outbreak in São Paulo, Brazil. The research aimed to assess whether vaccine effectiveness waned over time and whether a single dose was sufficient. A test-negative case-control study design was used, analyzing 166,390 tests, including 65,365 from cases and 101,025 from controls. The results showed sustained effectiveness of one dose against symptomatic dengue (73.8% at 270–364 days and 76.8% at 365 days or more) and hospitalisation (74.6% at 270–365 days). Two-dose protection remained stable, with effectiveness against symptomatic dengue at 59.2% (95% CI 56.1–62.0) after one dose and 73.1% (69.1–76.6) after two doses. Against hospitalisation, effectiveness was 74.6% (62.7–82.7) after one dose and 87.9% (73.0–94.6) after two doses. The findings suggest that a single dose may provide sustained protection, generating a hypothesis about dose reduction that requires further evaluation. The study highlights the importance of dengue vaccination as a public health measure, particularly in outbreak settings. The evidence is robust and comparable across different virus strains, including DENV-3, which became more prevalent in 2025.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热是一种日益严重的全球健康威胁。我们评估了 疫苗 在 2024 年至 2025 年期间对青少年有症状、病毒学确诊的登革热和登革热住院治疗的 1 年有效性,其中 DENV-1 和 DENV-2 在 2024 年占主导地位,随后在 2025 年增加了 DENV-3 传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们于2024年2月20日至2025年12月31日期间在圣保罗州的10-15岁青少年中进行了一项测试呈阴性的病例对照研究。我们对巴西圣保罗州2024年疫苗期间青少年中的TAK-003登革热疫苗进行了初步评估,显示出短期保护作用,但表明在第一次剂量的 90 天,并且评估第二次剂量对住院治疗的有效性的能力有限。
elements_zh.methods: 病例被定义为经病毒学证实的登革热急性发热性疾病发作,通过 NS1 抗原或 RT-PCR 检测在症状出现后 5 天内检测到。对照是测试阴性的急性发热性疾病发作。使用混合效应逻辑回归评估一剂或两剂 TAK-003 后 疫苗 的有效性。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们分析了 166,390 项测试:其中 65,365 项来自病例,101,025 项来自对照。疫苗 治疗一剂后对有症状登革热的有效性为 59.2%(95% CI 56.1-62.0),两剂后为 73.1%(69.1-76.6)。针对登革热住院治疗,接种一剂后的有效率为 74.6%(62.7-82.7),两剂后的有效性为 87.9%(73.0-94.6)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 单剂疫苗对有症状登革热的保护效果在1年随访期间未出现减弱迹象:在270–364天时为73.8%(64.7–80.6),在≥365天时为76.8%(59.3–86.8)。2剂疫苗的保护效果在1年内保持稳定(270–365天时为74.6%,95% CI 59.0–84.2)。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强化了登革热 疫苗接种 作为公共卫生措施的重要性。敏感性分析的结果是稳健的,并且在 DENV-3 循环增加期间具有可比性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 我们的研究结果表明,TAK-003 在大 暴发 期间对青少年有症状的登革热和登革热住院治疗具有持续 1 年的保护作用。所提供的证据没有报告任何具体限制。

title: Dual readout RT-LAMP for rapid on-site dengue virus detection and serotyping
abstract: ABSTRACT Dengue is the fastest-growing mosquito-borne disease, with over 14 million reported cases globally in 2024, rendering dengue a major public health issue of global concern. Fast and reliable serotype-specific diagnosis of dengue is critical for patient risk management and epidemiological surveillance. While real-time PCR currently remains the gold standard for dengue virus detection, it requires thermal cyclers and trained personnel in an established laboratory infrastructure, limiting its use in low-resource settings. Loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) offers a promising alternative, yet currently available reverse transcription assays for dengue either rely on limited sequences used for primer design, thus failing to adequately capture global genetic diversity, or use multiple primer sets, increasing complexity and costs. We developed four serotype-specific dengue virus (DENV) reverse transcription (RT)-LAMP assays in which primer design was informed by 4,277 whole-genome sequences from different geographical regions. Degenerate base positions were incorporated into primers to achieve broad detection capability while minimizing the number of distinct oligonucleotides needed. The assays achieved analytical sensitivities of 96–734 genome equivalents per reaction after 60 min. Clinical evaluation using 95 PCR-confirmed positive samples from Sri Lanka, including serotypes 1–3, demonstrated detection rates of 91.2% for DENV1, 78.6% for DENV2, and 100% for DENV3, with no cross-reactivity observed between serotypes. Evaluation using DENV4-spiked serum demonstrated reliable detection at clinically relevant viral loads, with complete detection at quantification cycle (Cq) values of ~30. A dual readout design enables both real-time fluorescence detection and equipment-free visual colorimetric detection, rendering the assays suitable for point-of-care applications in dengue-endemic regions worldwide. IMPORTANCE Dengue virus infections pose a growing threat to global health, with cases doubling annually since 2021, yet reliable diagnostic tools remain inaccessible in many affected regions. Current gold-standard molecular tests require expensive equipment and specialized laboratories, creating a critical gap in dengue-endemic areas where rapid, on-site diagnosis could save lives through early patient management and outbreak control. This study addresses this gap by developing dengue virus serotype-specific detection assays that work at a constant temperature without the need for sophisticated and expensive equipment. By analyzing thousands of dengue virus genome sequences and strategically incorporating degenerate bases, we designed primers that can detect diverse viral strains while maintaining simplicity and low cost. The assays provide results in 40–60 min, depending on the workflow, and can be read visually without instruments, making them practical for use in clinics, field settings, and resource-limited laboratories where dengue burden is highest.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a rapid, on-site dengue virus detection and serotyping method to address the limitations of current diagnostic tools. title_zh: 双读出 RT-LAMP,用于快速现场 登革病毒 检测和血清分型
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Dengue is the fastest-growing mosquito-borne disease, with over 14 million reported cases globally in 2024, rendering dengue a major public health issue of global concern. Fast and reliable serotype-specific diagnosis of dengue is critical for patient risk management and epidemiological surveillance. While real-time PCR currently remains the gold standard for dengue virus detection, it requires thermal cyclers and trained personnel in an established laboratory infrastructure, limiting its use in low-resource settings. Loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) offers a promising alternative, yet currently available reverse transcription assays for dengue either rely on limited sequences used for primer design, thus failing to adequately capture global genetic diversity, or use multiple primer sets, increasing complexity and costs. We developed four serotype-specific dengue virus (DENV) reverse transcription (RT)-LAMP assays in which primer design was informed by 4,277 whole-genome sequences from different geographical regions. Degenerate base positions were incorporated into primers to achieve broad detection capability while minimizing the number of distinct oligonucleotides needed. The assays achieved analytical sensitivities of 96–734 genome equivalents per reaction after 60 min. Clinical evaluation using 95 PCR-confirmed positive samples from Sri Lanka, including serotypes 1–3, demonstrated detection rates of 91.2% for DENV1, 78.6% for DENV2, and 100% for DENV3, with no cross-reactivity observed between serotypes. Evaluation using DENV4-spiked serum demonstrated reliable detection at clinically relevant viral loads, with complete detection at quantification cycle (Cq) values of ~30. A dual readout design enables both real-time fluorescence detection and equipment-free visual colorimetric detection, rendering the assays suitable for point-of-care applications in dengue-endemic regions worldwide. IMPORTANCE Dengue virus infections pose a growing threat to global health, with cases doubling annually since 2021, yet reliable diagnostic tools remain inaccessible in many affected regions. Current gold-standard molecular tests require expensive equipment and specialized laboratories, creating a critical gap in dengue-endemic areas where rapid, on-site diagnosis could save lives through early patient management and outbreak control. This study addresses this gap by developing dengue virus serotype-specific detection assays that work at a constant temperature without the need for sophisticated and expensive equipment. By analyzing thousands of dengue virus genome sequences and strategically incorporating degenerate bases, we designed primers that can detect diverse viral strains while maintaining simplicity and low cost. The assays provide results in 40–60 min, depending on the workflow, and can be read visually without instruments, making them practical for use in clinics, field settings, and resource-limited laboratories where dengue burden is highest.

title: Dengue Fever in India at a Crossroads: Spatiotemporal Trends, Climate Change, and Vaccine Challenges in the Post-COVID Era
abstract: Dengue fever is a major public health issue in India because its incidence and mortality rates vary with environmental, social, and infrastructural factors. There are not many effective vaccines yet, so the main treatments are supportive care, vector control, and surveillance. This study aimed to examine patterns in dengue cases and deaths across Indian states from 2023-2025, focusing on regional differences, the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and climate change, and the progress of vaccine development. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, dengue cases in India remained a significant public health concern. In 2023, India reported 289,235 dengue cases and 485 deaths. In 2024, the number of reported cases declined to 233,519, with 297 deaths. As of 30 November 2025, 113,540 dengue cases and 95 deaths had been reported. Throughout this period, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Karnataka consistently recorded the highest dengue burden. Urbanization and climate change were two of the main reasons. There are still only a few vaccines to choose from, and it’s not clear how safe and effective the live-attenuated vaccines (Dengvaxia® and Qdenga). Dengue remains a growing and evolving threat in India. A comprehensive solution must encompass environmental management, vaccine research, public health monitoring, and climate change adaptation.
journal: Journal of Pure and Applied Microbiology

elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用了 2023 年至 2025 年期间印度各邦报告的病例和死亡数据。它的重点是分析区域差异以及大流行和气候变化对登革热趋势的影响。数据来源于公共卫生记录,并分析其模式和相关性。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有必要继续开展 监测、环境管理和 疫苗 研究,以减轻印度登革热的影响。他们还强调气候变化在塑造登革热趋势中的作用。

source_body_en: Dengue fever is a major public health issue in India because its incidence and mortality rates vary with environmental, social, and infrastructural factors. There are not many effective vaccines yet, so the main treatments are supportive care, vector control, and surveillance. This study aimed to examine patterns in dengue cases and deaths across Indian states from 2023-2025, focusing on regional differences, the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and climate change, and the progress of vaccine development. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, dengue cases in India remained a significant public health concern. In 2023, India reported 289,235 dengue cases and 485 deaths. In 2024, the number of reported cases declined to 233,519, with 297 deaths. As of 30 November 2025, 113,540 dengue cases and 95 deaths had been reported. Throughout this period, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Karnataka consistently recorded the highest dengue burden. Urbanization and climate change were two of the main reasons. There are still only a few vaccines to choose from, and it’s not clear how safe and effective the live-attenuated vaccines (Dengvaxia® and Qdenga). Dengue remains a growing and evolving threat in India. A comprehensive solution must encompass environmental management, vaccine research, public health monitoring, and climate change adaptation.

title: Mapping Spatio-Temporal Hotspots of Dengue Transmission in Tasikmalaya, Indonesia.
abstract: BACKGROUND OBJECTIVES: Dengue is a major vector-borne disease in tropical and subtropical regions, including Indonesia, where recurrent outbreaks remain a significant public health concern. Understanding the spatial and temporal distribution of dengue transmission is essential for effective surveillance and targeted control strategies. This study aimed to map the spatio-temporal hotspots of dengue transmission in Tasikmalaya City, West Java, Indonesia, using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and spatial statistical analysis. METHODS: Village-level spatial analyses were conducted using reported dengue cases from the complete calendar year of 2022 and 279 cases reported between January and September 2023. Of the 279 cases reported in 2023, 275 had valid residential coordinates and were included in the space-time cluster analysis. The space-time analysis was based on symptom onset dates ranging from 27 December 2022 to 30 September 2023. Global Moran's I, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), bivariate LISA, and the spatial scan statistic implemented in SaTScan were used to assess the spatial distribution and spatio-temporal clustering of dengue cases. RESULTS: Spatial clustering of dengue cases was identified in several urban villages, particularly around Cipedes and Tugujaya. Bivariate LISA revealed significant spatial co-occurrence between high dengue incidence and high population density. Spatio-temporal analysis detected three statistically significant clusters during 2023, indicating that dengue transmission was concentrated in specific geographic areas during distinct periods rather than being uniformly distributed over time. INTERPRETATION CONCLUSION: The findings highlight distinct spatio-temporal hotspots of dengue transmission and emphasize the role of population density and seasonal factors in shaping dengue risk. Spatial mapping and cluster detection can support targeted vector control and public health interventions.

title: Epidemic Years Increase Hospitalization but Not Mortality Among Laboratory-Confirmed Dengue Cases in Mexico: A Nationwide Surveillance Study, 2020–2025
abstract: Dengue is a major public health problem in Mexico, where large epidemics have occurred during recent years. Although demographic and clinical predictors of severe dengue have been widely studied, the impact of epidemic transmission periods on hospitalization and mortality remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the association between epidemic years and hospitalization and mortality among laboratory-confirmed dengue cases in Mexico. A nationwide retrospective analytical study was conducted using laboratory-confirmed dengue cases reported through the Mexican National Epidemiological Surveillance System between 2020 and 2025. Years were classified as epidemic (2023–2024) or non-epidemic (2020–2022 and 2025) according to official endemic channel analyses. Hospitalization and mortality were evaluated as primary outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression models were developed to identify factors independently associated with hospitalization and mortality. A total of 235,226 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases were included, of whom 90,661 (38.5%) were hospitalized and 1604 (0.68%) died. Overall, 170,819 cases (72.6%) occurred during epidemic years. Hospitalization was more frequent during epidemic years than during non-epidemic years (40.2% vs. 34.1%; crude OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.27–1.32; p < 0.001), whereas mortality did not differ significantly (0.68% vs. 0.69%; crude OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.89–1.11; p = 0.919). In multivariable analysis, epidemic-year status remained independently associated with hospitalization (aOR 1.26, 95% CI 1.24–1.29; p < 0.001) but not with mortality (aOR 1.00, 95% CI 0.90–1.12; p = 0.946). Chronic kidney disease showed the strongest independent association with both hospitalization (aOR 5.36, 95% CI 4.33–6.65) and mortality (aOR 6.98, 95% CI 5.23–9.32). Advanced age and other underlying comorbidities were also independently associated with adverse outcomes. Epidemic years were associated with increased hospitalization among laboratory-confirmed dengue cases in Mexico but were not associated with increased mortality. Mortality was more strongly associated with age and underlying comorbidities, particularly chronic kidney disease. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening hospital preparedness during epidemic periods while prioritizing clinical monitoring of high-risk patients.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热是墨西哥的一个主要公共卫生问题,近年来该国曾发生大规模流行病。尽管 重症登革热 的人口统计学和临床​​预测因素已得到广泛研究,但流行病 传播 时期对住院治疗和 死亡率 的影响仍知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用墨西哥国家流行病学 监测 系统报告的 2020 年至 2025 年间实验室确诊的登革热病例进行了一项全国性回顾性分析研究。根据官方流行渠道分析,年份被分为流行期(2023-2024 年)或非流行期(2020-2022 年和 2025 年)。总共纳入了 235,226 例实验室确诊的登革热病例,其中 90,661 例(38.5%)住院治疗,1604 例(0.68%)死亡。
elements_zh.methods: 开发多变量逻辑回归模型来识别与住院和 死亡率 独立相关的因素。住院治疗和 死亡率 作为主要结局进行评估。
elements_zh.main_results: Hospitalization was more frequent during epidemic years than during non-epidemic years (40.2% vs. 34.1%; crude OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.27–1.32; p < 0.001), whereas mortality did not differ significantly (0.68% vs. 0.69%; crude OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.89–1.11; p = 0.919). In multivariable analysis, epidemic-year status remained independently associated with hospitalization (aOR 1.26, 95% CI 1.24–1.29; p < 0.001) but not with mortality (aOR 1.00, 95% CI 0.90–1.12; p = 0.946).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 流行年份与墨西哥实验室确诊登革热病例住院率的增加有关,但与 死亡率 的增加无关。这些发现强调了在流行期间加强医院准备工作的重要性,同时优先考虑对高危患者的临床监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 死亡率 与年龄和潜在合并症(尤其是慢性肾脏病)的相关性更强。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。该研究是一项全国性的监测研究,样本量大,统计分析清晰,证据强度高。

title: Dengue Virus Molecular Targets and Antiviral Drug Development: Advances, Challenges and Therapeutic Perspectives
abstract: ABSTRACT Dengue is the most prevalent arboviral disease in tropical and subtropical regions, with over 13 million cases recorded in the Americas in 2024. Despite its enormous public health impact, no specific antiviral therapy is currently approved for dengue virus (DENV). In this context, this narrative review critically analyses the principal molecular targets of DENV, including structural proteins (C, prM/M and E), nonstructural proteins (NS1–NS5) and host factors, with emphasis on the development of small‐molecule antivirals and an evaluation of their progress in pre‐clinical and clinical studies. The NS2B–NS3 protease complex and NS5 (both RdRp and MTase domains) remain the most extensively explored targets, owing to the availability of high‐resolution crystal structures and higher inter‐serotype conservation. NS4B has emerged as the most clinically advanced target. Among direct‐acting antivirals, AT‐752 was also discontinued due to low viraemia at enrolment, while NITD‐688 remains among the most advanced pipeline molecules. Host‐directed therapies including anakinra and baricitinib are under clinical investigation for severe dengue. Key translational challenges include viral serotype diversity, pharmacokinetic limitations, cytotoxicity, and the timing of treatment initiation relative to viral kinetics. Advances in rational drug design, drug repurposing, allosteric inhibition, and targeted protein degradation (PROTACs) offer renewed perspectives for effective dengue therapeutics.
authors: Aryane Lucia da Silva Aguiar De Oliveira
Marcelo Arthur Dias da Costa Santana

In this context, this narrative review critically analyses the principal molecular targets of DENV, including structural proteins (C, prM/M and E), nonstructural proteins (NS1–NS5) and host factors, with emphasis on the development of small‐molecule antivirals and an evaluation of their progress in pre‐clinical and clinical studies. The NS2B–NS3 protease complex and NS5 (both RdRp and MTase domains) remain the most extensively explored targets, owing to the availability of high‐resolution crystal structures and higher inter‐serotype conservation. NS4B has emerged as the most clinically advanced target. Among direct‐acting antivirals, AT‐752 was also discontinued due to low viraemia at enrolment, while NITD‐688 remains among the most advanced pipeline molecules. Host‐directed therapies including anakinra and baricitinib are under clinical investigation for severe dengue. Key translational challenges include viral serotype diversity, pharmacokinetic limitations, cytotoxicity, and the timing of treatment initiation relative to viral kinetics. Advances in rational drug design, drug repurposing, allosteric inhibition, and targeted protein degradation (PROTACs) offer renewed perspectives for effective dengue therapeutics.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the molecular targets of dengue virus (DENV) and their relevance to antiviral drug development. It highlights the NS2B–NS3 protease complex and NS5 as the most extensively studied targets due to their structural availability and conservation across serotypes. NS4B is noted as the most clinically advanced target. The review identifies challenges such as serotype diversity, pharmacokinetic limitations, and cytotoxicity, while emphasizing the potential of rational drug design, drug repurposing, and PROTACs. It also notes that AT-752 was discontinued, and NITD-688 remains a promising candidate. Host-directed therapies like anakinra and baricitinib are under investigation for severe dengue. The review underscores the need for further research and development to address these challenges and improve therapeutic options for dengue.

title: Prevalence of Severe Dengue Infection in Bangladesh: A Bayesian Meta-analysis
abstract: Severe dengue represents a critical and potentially life-threatening stage of dengue infection, often characterizes by internal bleeding which leads to death. Several studies existed on severe dengue but a meta-analysis can provide robust understanding of the epidemiology of the disease. This study aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of dengue cases which developed to severe dengue in Bangladesh. A systematic literature search was conducted across five databases between January 2000 and June 2025: PubMed, Google Scholar, Cochrane Central, Science Direct, and BanglaJOL. After title and abstract screening and full text review, this study included 41 cross-sectional studies. The quality of included studies were assessed using the STROBE checklist. Bayesian random-effects model was applied to estimate the pooled prevalence, with both non-informative and informative priors. Further, model diagnostics including trace plots and autocorrelation checks were used to assess MCMC convergence. A Bayesian random-effects model using the strongly informative prior estimated a pooled prevalence of 33.9% (95% Credible Interval: 25.4, 42.0), and a between-study heterogeneity () of 0.074. Model diagnostics were further supported these findings by the evidence of adequate mixing and convergence, with no signs of autocorrelation in the MCMC chains. However, this study have found one-third of the dengue cases developed to severe dengue cases which indicates a serious burden for the healthcare system of the country. These findings have important implications for public health surveillance and can inform policymakers in planning and prioritizing interventions to manage severe dengue cases in Bangladesh. 74(2): 301–310, 2026 (July)

title_original: Prevalence of Severe Dengue Infection in Bangladesh: A Bayesian Meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the prevalence of severe dengue infection in Bangladesh, focusing on the proportion of dengue cases progressing to severe dengue, a life-threatening stage characterized by internal bleeding and potential fatality.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic literature search across five databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, Cochrane Central, Science Direct, and BanglaJOL) from January 2000 to June 2025, identifying 41 cross-sectional studies. Study quality was assessed using the STROBE checklist, and a Bayesian random-effects model with both non-informative and informative priors was applied to estimate pooled prevalence.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled prevalence of severe dengue among dengue cases in Bangladesh was estimated at 33.9% (95% Credible Interval: 25.4, 42.0), with a between-study heterogeneity (τ2) of 0.074. Model diagnostics confirmed adequate mixing and convergence of MCMC chains, with no signs of autocorrelation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report the geographic or temporal distribution of included studies, limiting insights into regional or seasonal variations in severe dengue prevalence. Additionally, the reliance on cross-sectional studies may introduce selection bias, and the use of a Bayesian model with informative priors could influence pooled estimates.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The high pooled prevalence of severe dengue (33.9%) underscores a significant burden on Bangladesh's healthcare system, necessitating targeted public health surveillance and resource allocation. Policymakers should prioritize interventions to manage severe dengue cases, including early diagnosis and treatment strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review estimates that approximately one-third of dengue cases in Bangladesh progress to severe dengue, a life-threatening condition marked by internal bleeding. Using a Bayesian meta-analysis of 41 cross-sectional studies identified through a systematic search of five databases (2000–2025), the pooled prevalence of severe dengue was 33.9% (95% Credible Interval: 25.4–42.0), with low between-study heterogeneity (τ2 = 0.074). Model diagnostics confirmed robust convergence and mixing of Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations. The findings highlight a substantial healthcare burden, emphasizing the need for enhanced surveillance and targeted interventions to mitigate severe dengue outcomes in Bangladesh.

title: Meteorological drivers and short-term prediction of dengue fever in a tropical region of China: evidence from Hainan Province
abstract: Objective Meteorological factors influence dengue transmission through nonlinear and lagged effects. This study assessed these associations in Hainan Province and developed an early risk prediction index. Methods Weekly dengue case and meteorological data from Hainan Province (2018–2019 and 2023–2024) were analyzed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs). An early risk prediction index(ERPI) was constructed from DLNM-derived cumulative meteorological risk signals and imported cases. Predictive performance was evaluated using leave-one-year-out cross-validation and assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results Among 927 dengue cases reported during the four modelled years, 727 (78.43%) were locally acquired. Weekly mean daily maximum temperature (Tmax), precipitation (Pmean), wind speed (WSmean), and diurnal temperature range (DTRmean) showed nonlinear, lag-dependent associations with dengue risk, with distinct temporal patterns. Higher Tmax showed longer-lag effects, peaking at 33.73 °C at lag 8 weeks ( RR = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.70–3.63). Its cumulative effect was strongest over lags 5–8 weeks, peaking at approximately 32 °C. Pmean showed a nonlinear association, peaking at 4 mm/day at a lag of 4 weeks ( RR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.59–2.31), with significant cumulative effect across both the 1–4- and 5–8-week windows. Low WSmean and moderate DTRmean showed their strongest cumulative associations over lags 1–4 weeks, peaking at 2.0 m/s and 6.1 °C, respectively. These harmful associations attenuated over lags 5–8 weeks, whereas higher WSmean and DTRmean were generally protective. The ERPI predicted local dengue occurrence within the subsequent 1–4-week windows, with AUCs of 0.762–0.843. Across these windows, sensitivities were 0.768–0.797, specificities were 0.644–0.708, PPVs were 0.468–0.624, and NPVs were 0.822–0.911. Conclusion In Hainan, high temperature was primarily associated with medium-to-long-term dengue risk, whereas low-to-moderate diurnal temperature range increased short-term risk. Precipitation was associated with risk across both short and medium-to-long lags, while cumulative wind-speed associations were strongest over shorter lags and attenuated thereafter. The DLNM-based early risk prediction index may support meteorology-informed early warning and dengue control in tropical settings, although requiring external validation is needed before operational implementation.

title_zh: 中国热带地区登革热的气象驱动因素和短期预测:来自海南省的证据
source_body_en: Objective Meteorological factors influence dengue transmission through nonlinear and lagged effects. This study assessed these associations in Hainan Province and developed an early risk prediction index. Methods Weekly dengue case and meteorological data from Hainan Province (2018–2019 and 2023–2024) were analyzed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs). An early risk prediction index(ERPI) was constructed from DLNM-derived cumulative meteorological risk signals and imported cases. Predictive performance was evaluated using leave-one-year-out cross-validation and assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results Among 927 dengue cases reported during the four modelled years, 727 (78.43%) were locally acquired. Weekly mean daily maximum temperature (Tmax), precipitation (Pmean), wind speed (WSmean), and diurnal temperature range (DTRmean) showed nonlinear, lag-dependent associations with dengue risk, with distinct temporal patterns. Higher Tmax showed longer-lag effects, peaking at 33.73 °C at lag 8 weeks ( RR = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.70–3.63). Its cumulative effect was strongest over lags 5–8 weeks, peaking at approximately 32 °C. Pmean showed a nonlinear association, peaking at 4 mm/day at a lag of 4 weeks ( RR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.59–2.31), with significant cumulative effect across both the 1–4- and 5–8-week windows. Low WSmean and moderate DTRmean showed their strongest cumulative associations over lags 1–4 weeks, peaking at 2.0 m/s and 6.1 °C, respectively. These harmful associations attenuated over lags 5–8 weeks, whereas higher WSmean and DTRmean were generally protective. The ERPI predicted local dengue occurrence within the subsequent 1–4-week windows, with AUCs of 0.762–0.843. Across these windows, sensitivities were 0.768–0.797, specificities were 0.644–0.708, PPVs were 0.468–0.624, and NPVs were 0.822–0.911. Conclusion In Hainan, high temperature was primarily associated with medium-to-long-term dengue risk, whereas low-to-moderate diurnal temperature range increased short-term risk. Precipitation was associated with risk across both short and medium-to-long lags, while cumulative wind-speed associations were strongest over shorter lags and attenuated thereafter. The DLNM-based early risk prediction index may support meteorology-informed early warning and dengue control in tropical settings, although requiring external validation is needed before operational implementation.

title: Applying AI Embodied Deep Learning Models for Real‐Time Prediction and Classification of Dengue Virus Serotypes Using Complete Genome Data
abstract: Designed for the serotype categorization and sequence generation of Dengue Virus (DE VI ), using whole genome data, this study presents an AI embodied deep learning system, AIemDL DVE . We constructed unified datasets using processed 2000 genome sequences and built an LSTM-based generative model capable of identifying distinct characteristics in DE VI sequences. Comparative analysis of GRU, 1 Dimensional convolutional analysis (1D-Con), and Simple RNN models found that the LSTM model produced sequences surpassing 10 kb with great precision, therefore revealing its improved performance. With a feed-forward neural network (FNN), we categorized with an F1 score of 99% and validation accuracy of 98.12%. Moreover, motif analysis underscored conserved genetic components using the MEME Suite highlighted, which enhances model interpretability. Although it is most pertinent to similar-sized genomes, our AIemDL DVE method provides reliable predictions that might help DE VI -related vaccine research and diagnostics. This work demonstrates how effectively AI embodied deep learning may improve viral sequence classification and support knowledge of viral evolution and spread.

title: Tinjauan Pelaksanaan Surveilans Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever Rawat Inap di Rumah Sakit Marinir Cilandak
abstract: In 2022, Indonesia recorded a total of 131,265 Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) cases, with 40% occurring in children aged 0-14 years. Preliminary observations conducted in December 2022 at Cilandak Marine Hospital revealed that while surveillance was performed daily, it was frequently delayed. Reporting lags in data collection were attributed to limited human resources, as there was only one dedicated staff member who was frequently assigned to external duties. This study employs a qualitative descriptive method to illustrate the implementation of the DHF surveillance system at Cilandak Marine Hospital. Results from observations and interviews with medical record officers indicate that there is no Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for DHF surveillance. Data analysis regarding the timeliness of reporting for hospitalized DHF patients showed a rate of only 7.6% (out of 13 patients) in March, compared to 50% (out of 4 patients) in October. Furthermore, daily attendance for active hospital surveillance was recorded at only 3.3% in March 2023 and 6.5% in October, indicating low compliance with surveillance performance indicators. Timeliness in data collection and submission is critical as an early warning indicator to prevent the widespread transmission of dengue and the occurrence of outbreaks (Extraordinary Events).
journal: Detector: Jurnal Inovasi Riset Ilmu Kesehatan

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the implementation of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) surveillance in hospitals to address the public health problem of dengue disease, which is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in children.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at Cilandak Marine Hospital in December 2022 and March/October 2023, focusing on hospitalized DHF patients and the daily surveillance practices implemented there.
analysis.methods: The study used a qualitative descriptive method involving observations and interviews with medical record officers to assess the implementation of DHF surveillance and identify challenges in data collection and reporting.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the lack of standardized procedures and low compliance with surveillance performance indicators, indicating a need for improved systems to ensure timely data collection and reporting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results emphasize the importance of timely data collection and submission for early warning and outbreak prevention, which can inform better surveillance strategies in dengue-endemic areas.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用定性描述方法,包括观察和采访病历官员,以评估 DHF 监测 的实施情况,并确定数据收集和报告方面的挑战。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 调查结果强调了缺乏标准化程序以及对 监测 绩效指标的遵守率低,这表明需要改进系统以确保及时的数据收集和报告。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了及时收集和提交数据对于早期预警和 监测 预防的重要性,这可以为登革热流行地区更好的 监测 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于观察和访谈,这可能会引入偏差。证据是中等的,因为它提供了对 监测 实践的见解,但缺乏更广泛影响的定量数据。

title: Longitudinal changes in platelet indices during recovery from dengue fever: A prospective observational study
abstract: Background: Dengue fever, caused by the flavivirus, is a major health problem in tropical regions. Severe infection presents with thrombocytopenia, hemoconcentration, and bleeding manifestations. Platelet indices, including mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), plateletcrit (PCT), platelet large cell count (P-LCC), and platelet large cell ratio (P-LCR), have been proposed as potential markers of disease activity in dengue fever; however, their longitudinal behavior remains uncertain. Aims and Objectives: This study was undertaken to determine and assess the role of different platelet indices (MPV, PDW-standard deviation, PDW-coefficient of variation, P-LCC, P-LCR) in dengue fever and to determine the correlation between the clinical course and outcome of dengue fever with the platelet indices. Materials and Methods: This prospective study included 53 serologically confirmed dengue patients over 6 months. Clinical data were collected. Platelet count, MPV, PDW, PCT, P-LCC, P-LCR, and hematocrit (HCT) were measured at 12-h intervals. Repeated measures analysis and linear mixed-effects modeling evaluated longitudinal trends. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis assessed the association and predictive performance for moderate/poor clinical conditions. Results: The study included 42 males (79.2%), 11 females (20.8%), with mean age of 32.1 years. Most cases were of dengue without warning signs as per the World Health Organization 2009 classification. Platelet counts increased during hospitalization (P<0.001). MPV demonstrated an upward trend over time (β=0.542 fL/day, P<0.001). Higher MPV was associated with lower odds of moderate/poor clinical condition (odds ratio 0.68, P=0.017). However, ROC analysis showed limited standalone discriminative ability (area under the curve=0.33). PDW, P-LCC, and P-LCR showed recovery-phase increases, while HCT declined. Conclusion: Platelet indices demonstrate significant dynamic changes during recovery from dengue and may serve as adjunct markers of hematological regeneration. However, their independent predictive accuracy for clinical severity requires validation in larger cohorts.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热 由黄病毒引起,是热带地区的一个主要健康问题。严重感染表现为血小板减少、血液浓缩和出血表现。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前瞻性观察性研究纳入了 53 名血清学确诊的登革热患者,历时 6 个月。该研究包括 42 名男性(79.2%)、11 名女性(20.8%),平均年龄为 32.1 岁。根据世界卫生组织 2009 年的分类,大多数病例都是没有警告信号的登革热病例。
elements_zh.methods: 收集临床数据。每隔 12 小时测量一次血小板计数、MPV、PDW、PCT、P-LCC、P-LCR 和血细胞比容 (HCT)。重复测量分析和线性混合效应模型评估了纵向趋势。逻辑回归和受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析评估了中度/不良临床状况的关联性和预测性能。
elements_zh.main_results: 住院期间血小板计数增加(P<0.001)。MPV 随着时间的推移呈上升趋势(β=0.542 fL/天,P<0.001)。较高的 MPV 与中等/较差临床状况的几率较低相关(优势比 0.68,P=0.017)。然而,ROC 分析显示独立判别能力有限(曲线下面积 = 0.33)。PDW、P-LCC 和 P-LCR 显示恢复期增加,而 HCT 下降。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 血小板指数显示出登革热恢复期间显着的动态变化,并且可以作为血液再生的辅助标志物。它们对临床严重程度的独立预测准确性需要在更大的 队列研究 中进行验证。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于使用血小板指数作为辅助标记物来监测登革热恢复期间的血液再生。他们强调需要进一步验证这些指标以预测临床严重程度。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的样本量有限,且 ROC 分析的曲线下面积较低,表明证据是中等的。

title: A study of proteinuria and urine protein-creatinine ratio as a tool in predicting disease severity and adverse outcome in paediatric dengue fever
abstract: Objectives: Dengue fever presents with a wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, which range from mild febrile illness to severe forms such as dengue haemorrhagic fever and dengue shock syndrome. However, they emphasize the need for further large-scale studies to validate their predictive utility. The findings are relevant for improving surveillance and management strategies in paediatric dengue patients.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热 具有广泛的临床表现,从轻度发热性疾病到登革出血热和登革休克综合征等严重形式。早期识别更有可能发展为严重疾病的患者对于及时干预和适当的管理至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对三级医疗中心住院部的 90 名登革热 血清学 阳性儿科患者进行了一项前瞻性观察研究。该研究共纳入了 90 名年龄在 1 个月至 18 岁之间、经血清学证实患有登革热的儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 在临床怀疑登革热的基础上,进行了登革热血清学(非结构蛋白1抗原和免疫球蛋白M抗体)和全血细胞计数。连续 5 天每天测量蛋白尿和 UPCR,以及患者生命体征。
elements_zh.main_results: 38.89% 的儿童不存在蛋白尿,并且在 A 类中更为常见,而较高级别(2+ 和 3+)主要在 C 类中出现,与疾病严重程度呈显着正相关(r = 0.35,p = 0.001)。UPCR 平均峰值在患病第 4.04 ± 1.34 天记录。UPCR 水平升高 (>3) 与警告信号、低血压、出血表现、正性肌力支持需求、儿科重症监护病房入院和 死亡率 显着相关 (p < 0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 重症患者和预后较差的患者的 UPCR 峰值和蛋白尿值较高。尿蛋白评估,尤其是 UPCR,是确定登革热儿童疾病严重程度的重要标志。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 蛋白尿和 UPCR 升高与 重症登革热 和儿童不良临床结果显着相关。蛋白尿和 UPCR 都是简单且无创的参数,可能有助于早期风险分层。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。由于该研究基于明确的人群和明确的统计关联,因此研究结果的可信度很高。

Therefore, the present study aims to evaluate proteinuria and urine protein-creatinine ratio (UPCR) as indicators for predicting the severity of dengue and adverse outcomes in paediatric dengue patients. Material and Methods: Approval from the institutional ethics committee was obtained. Informed consent from the parents of participating subjects was obtained. We conducted a prospective observational study among 90 paediatric patients with positive dengue serology in the inpatient department of a tertiary care centre. On the basis of clinical suspicion of dengue, dengue serology (non-structural protein 1 antigen and immunoglobulin M antibody) and complete blood count were performed. Proteinuria and UPCR were measured daily for 5 days, along with patient vitals. Peak UPCR values were compared with dengue patients without warning signs, with warning signs and severe dengue. Results: A total of 90 children aged between 1 month and 18 years with serologically confirmed dengue were included in the study. The mean age was 7.9 ± 4.5 years, and no significant relationship was found between age and disease severity ( p = 0.698). Males accounted for 55.6% of the cases, and gender was not significantly associated with severity ( p = 0.479). Based on World Health Organization classification, 47.78% of cases were categorised as Category A, 24.44% as Category B and 27.78% as Category C. Proteinuria was absent in 38.89% of children and was more commonly observed in Category A, whereas higher grades (2+ and 3+) were predominantly seen in Category C, showing a significant positive correlation with disease severity (r = 0.35, p = 0.001). The mean peak UPCR was recorded on day 4.04 ± 1.34 of illness. Elevated UPCR levels (>3) were significantly associated with warning signs, hypotension, bleeding manifestations, need for inotropic support, paediatric intensive care unit admission and mortality ( p < 0.001). Overall, increasing UPCR levels were strongly linked to severe dengue and poorer clinical outcomes. Conclusion: Proteinuria and elevated UPCR are significantly associated with severe dengue and adverse clinical outcomes in children. Higher values of peak UPCR and proteinuria were seen in patients in the severe category and those with poorer outcomes. Assessment of urinary protein, especially the UPCR, serves as a valuable marker for determining disease severity in children with dengue. Both proteinuria and UPCR are simple and noninvasive parameters and may aid in early risk stratification; however, further large-scale studies are required to validate their predictive utility.

title: Comprehensive conservation profiling enables a robust multiplex RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous pan-detection and serotype discrimination of dengue virus
abstract: ABSTRACT Dengue virus (DENV) remains a critical global health threat, necessitating rapid pan-detection and precise serotyping. In this study, we developed a multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous detection and identification of DENV1–4. Guided by a systematic genomic conservation analysis of 4,754 sequences, we targeted the highly conserved 5′ untranslated region (5′ UTR) to design one pan-DENV and four serotype-specific primer-probe sets. The assay demonstrated robust analytical performance, with the limit of detection (LOD) ranging from 15.8 to 1.58 × 10 3 copies/mL and the lowest LOD (15.8 copies/mL) observed for serotype I with specific primer-probe sets. There was no cross-reactivity with other common pathogens of the Orthoflavivirus or Alphavirus genus pathogens , and clinical specificity was further validated as 100% using a negative cohort of non-dengue febrile samples. Validation using 53 clinical DENV-positive samples showed 100% concordance with a reference diagnostic kit for serotype identification. While the pan-DENV set served as a high-specificity screening tool with broad reactivity, it exhibited a clinical sensitivity of 88.7%, particularly missing low-titer samples (Ct > 30). This discrepancy, coupled with the superior sensitivity of the serotype-specific sets, suggests the presence of incomplete genomic fragments in acute-phase sera, highlighting the advantage of our 5′ UTR-targeted approach in assessing viral genomic integrity. This dual-layered multiplex assay provides a robust, rapid, and cost-effective tool for clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance. IMPORTANCE Dengue fever is a leading cause of systemic viral disease worldwide. Co-circulation of four distinct serotypes complicates clinical management and increases severe disease risk. Here, we presented a novel multiplex RT-qPCR assay enabling simultaneous pan-DENV detection and serotype identification in two tubes, comprising six reactions including an internal control (IC), thereby streamlining dengue diagnosis. A key innovation is the systematic selection of the 5′ UTR as the diagnostic target, guided by big-data genomic analysis. Unlike assays targeting the 3′ UTR, which may overrepresent viral loads by capturing redundant subgenomic orthoflavivirus RNA (sfRNA), our 5′ UTR-targeted design provides a more stringent measure of genomic integrity. Furthermore, the modular performance of our assay combining broad screening via a pan-DENV set with high-sensitivity subtyping which offers a dual-layer diagnostic framework. This work provides a high-performance tool for timely clinical intervention and enhances our molecular understanding of DENV fragments in clinical specimens.

title_zh: 全面的保守性分析可实现强大的多重 RT-qPCR 检测,可同时进行 登革病毒 的泛检测和血清型区分
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Dengue virus (DENV) remains a critical global health threat, necessitating rapid pan-detection and precise serotyping. In this study, we developed a multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous detection and identification of DENV1–4. Guided by a systematic genomic conservation analysis of 4,754 sequences, we targeted the highly conserved 5′ untranslated region (5′ UTR) to design one pan-DENV and four serotype-specific primer-probe sets. The assay demonstrated robust analytical performance, with the limit of detection (LOD) ranging from 15.8 to 1.58 × 10 3 copies/mL and the lowest LOD (15.8 copies/mL) observed for serotype I with specific primer-probe sets. There was no cross-reactivity with other common pathogens of the Orthoflavivirus or Alphavirus genus pathogens , and clinical specificity was further validated as 100% using a negative cohort of non-dengue febrile samples. Validation using 53 clinical DENV-positive samples showed 100% concordance with a reference diagnostic kit for serotype identification. While the pan-DENV set served as a high-specificity screening tool with broad reactivity, it exhibited a clinical sensitivity of 88.7%, particularly missing low-titer samples (Ct > 30). This discrepancy, coupled with the superior sensitivity of the serotype-specific sets, suggests the presence of incomplete genomic fragments in acute-phase sera, highlighting the advantage of our 5′ UTR-targeted approach in assessing viral genomic integrity. This dual-layered multiplex assay provides a robust, rapid, and cost-effective tool for clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance. IMPORTANCE Dengue fever is a leading cause of systemic viral disease worldwide. Co-circulation of four distinct serotypes complicates clinical management and increases severe disease risk. Here, we presented a novel multiplex RT-qPCR assay enabling simultaneous pan-DENV detection and serotype identification in two tubes, comprising six reactions including an internal control (IC), thereby streamlining dengue diagnosis. A key innovation is the systematic selection of the 5′ UTR as the diagnostic target, guided by big-data genomic analysis. Unlike assays targeting the 3′ UTR, which may overrepresent viral loads by capturing redundant subgenomic orthoflavivirus RNA (sfRNA), our 5′ UTR-targeted design provides a more stringent measure of genomic integrity. Furthermore, the modular performance of our assay combining broad screening via a pan-DENV set with high-sensitivity subtyping which offers a dual-layer diagnostic framework. This work provides a high-performance tool for timely clinical intervention and enhances our molecular understanding of DENV fragments in clinical specimens.
abstract_zh: 摘要 登革病毒 (DENV) 仍然是一个严重的全球健康威胁,需要快速的泛检测和精确的血清分型。在本研究中,我们开发了一种多重实时 RT-qPCR 检测方法,用于同时检测和鉴定 DENV1-4。在对 4,754 个序列进行系统性基因组保守性分析的指导下,我们针对高度保守的 5' 非翻译区 (5' UTR) 设计了一套泛 DENV 和四种血清型特异性引物探针组。该检测显示出强大的分析性能,检测限 (LOD) 范围为 15.8 至 1.58 × 10 3 拷贝/mL,并且使用特定引物-探针组观察到血清型 I 的最低 LOD(15.8 拷贝/mL)。与正黄病毒或甲病毒属病原体的其他常见病原体没有交叉反应,并且使用非登革热样本的阴性 队列研究 进一步验证临床特异性为 100%。使用 53 个临床 DENV 阳性样本进行的验证显示,与血清型鉴定的参考诊断试剂盒 100% 一致。虽然泛 DENV 组作为具有广泛反应性的高特异性筛查工具,但其临床敏感性为 88.7%,特别是缺失低滴度样本 (Ct > 30)。这种差异,加上血清型特异性组的卓越灵敏度,表明急性期血清中存在不完整的基因组片段,突出了我们的 5'UTR 靶向方法在评估病毒基因组完整性方面的优势。这种双层多重检测为临床 诊断 和流行病学 监测 提供了强大、快速且经济高效的工具。重要性 登革热 是全球系统性病毒性疾病的主要原因。四种不同血清型的共同循环使临床管理变得复杂并增加了严重疾病的风险。在这里,我们提出了一种新型多重 RT-qPCR 检测,可在两个试管中同时进行泛 DENV 检测和血清型鉴定,包括六个反应,包括内部对照 (IC),从而简化登革热 诊断。一项关键创新是在大数据基因组分析的指导下,系统地选择 5'UTR 作为诊断靶点。与针对 3'UTR 的检测不同,3'UTR 可能通过捕获冗余的亚基因组正黄病毒 RNA (sfRNA) 来过度代表病毒载量,我们的 5'UTR 靶向设计提供了更严格的基因组完整性测量。此外,我们的检测的模块化性能将通过泛 DENV 集进行的广泛筛选与高灵敏度亚型相结合,提供了双层诊断框架。这项工作为及时临床干预提供了高性能工具,并增强了我们对临床标本中 DENV 片段的分子理解。

title: Analisis Faktor yang Berhubungan dengan Angka Kejadian Demam Berdarah Dengue di Kelurahan Menteng Kota Palangka Raya
abstract: ABSTRACT Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever remains a major public health problem in Indonesia, with increasing incidence in Palangka Raya City. This study aimed to analyze factors associated with the incidence of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever in Menteng Subdistrict, Palangka Raya City. An analytical observational study with a case-control design was conducted involving 130 respondents with a 1:1 ratio between case and control groups. Data were collected through interviews using structured questionnaires and direct observation using checklists. Statistical analysis was performed using Chi-Square tests. The results showed no significant association between knowledge and Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever incidence (p=1.000). However, attitude (p=0.002), water storage conditions (p=0.008), and housing conditions (p=0.011) were significantly associated with the incidence. Attitude and poor housing conditions increased the risk of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever, while proper water storage acted as a protective factor. In conclusion, attitude, water storage conditions, and housing conditions are significantly associated with Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever incidence in Menteng Subdistrict, Palangka Raya City. Keywords: Attitude, Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever, Housing Condition, Knowledge, Water Storage. ABSTRAK Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) tetap menjadi masalah kesehatan masyarakat yang serius di Indonesia, dengan angka kejadian yang terus meningkat di Kota Palangka Raya. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis faktor-faktor yang terkait dengan kejadian Demam Berdarah Dengue di Kecamatan Menteng, Kota Palangka Raya. Penelitian observasional analitis dengan desain kasus-kontrol dilakukan dengan melibatkan 130 responden dengan rasio 1:1 antara kelompok kasus dan kelompok kontrol. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara menggunakan kuesioner terstruktur dan observasi langsung menggunakan daftar periksa. Analisis statistik dilakukan menggunakan uji Chi-Square. Hasil menunjukkan tidak ada hubungan yang signifikan antara pengetahuan dan kejadian Demam Berdarah Dengue (p=1,000). Namun, sikap (p=0,002), kondisi penyimpanan air (p=0,008), dan kondisi perumahan (p=0,011) secara signifikan terkait dengan insidensi. Sikap dan kondisi perumahan yang buruk meningkatkan risiko Demam Berdarah Dengue, sedangkan penyimpanan air yang baik berperan sebagai faktor pelindung. Kesimpulannya, sikap, kondisi penyimpanan air, dan kondisi perumahan secara signifikan terkait dengan kejadian Demam Berdarah Dengue di Kecamatan Menteng, Kota Palangka Raya. Kata Kunci: Sikap, Demam Berdarah Dengue, Kondisi Rumah, Pengetahuan, Penyimpanan Air.

analysis.study_design_and_population: An analytical observational study with a case-control design was conducted involving 130 respondents with a 1:1 ratio between case and control groups. analysis.methods: Statistical analysis was performed using Chi-Square tests. Analisis statistik dilakukan menggunakan uji Chi-Square.
analysis.main_results: The results showed no significant association between knowledge and Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever incidence (p=1.000). However, attitude (p=0.002), water storage conditions (p=0.008), and housing conditions (p=0.011) were significantly associated with the incidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Attitude and poor housing conditions increased the risk of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever, while proper water storage acted as a protective factor. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted public health interventions aimed at improving attitudes, water storage practices, and housing conditions to reduce the incidence of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever in Menteng Subdistrict.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and its abstract-only nature. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational design and lack of longitudinal or experimental data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates factors associated with Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever incidence in Menteng Subdistrict, Palangka Raya City, Indonesia. Attitude and poor housing conditions increase the risk, while proper water storage acts as a protective factor. The study highlights the importance of behavioral and environmental factors in disease transmission. However, its reliance on self-reported data and observational nature limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革出血热仍然是印度尼西亚的一个主要公共卫生问题,帕朗卡拉亚市的 发病率 病例不断增加。本研究旨在分析帕朗卡拉雅市门腾街道登革出血热 发病率 的相关因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 进行了一项采用病例对照设计的分析观察研究,涉及 130 名受访者,病例组与对照组的比例为 1:1。数据通过使用结构化问卷的访谈和使用清单的直接观察来收集。
elements_zh.methods: 使用卡方检验进行统计分析。分析统计数据并分析 uji 卡方。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示知识与登革出血热 发病率 之间没有显着关联 (p=1.000)。然而,态度(p=0.002)、储水条件(p=0.008)和住房条件(p=0.011)与发病率显着相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 态度和恶劣的住房条件增加了登革出血热的风险,而适当的储水则起到了保护因素的作用。研究结果强调了行为和环境因素在登革出血热 传播 动态中的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为旨在改善态度、储水做法和住房条件的有针对性的公共卫生干预措施提供信息,以减少门腾街道登革出血热的 发病率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对自我报告数据的依赖和纯抽象的性质而受到限制。由于观察设计和缺乏纵向或实验数据,证据强度中等。

title: Synthesis and Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Evaluation of Novel 1,2,3-Triazole–Quinoline Derivatives Targeting SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, DENV-2, and CHIKV
abstract: The persistent global threat posed by emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, DENV-2, and CHIKV, highlights the critical need for novel and broad-spectrum antiviral agents. Building upon the established antiviral activity of the quinoline scaffold, this study employed a molecular hybridization strategy to design and synthesize a novel series of 1,2,3-triazole–quinoline derivatives (compounds 4a–4h). This approach strategically fused the bioactive quinoline nucleus with the pharmaceutically favorable 1,2,3-triazole ring. The new compounds were synthesized efficiently in three steps with moderate-to-high yields, and their structures were subsequently determined. Their inhibitory capacities against the four viruses and cytotoxicity across relevant cell lines were evaluated in vitro. The initial screening demonstrated that compounds 4a–4h possessed broad-spectrum antiviral activity, showing high inhibition percentages at 10 μM against SARS-CoV-2, DENV-2, and CHIKV. Notably, compounds 4c and 4e, substituted with methoxy and ethyl groups, respectively, displayed exceptional potency and safety against SARS-CoV-2, yielding high selectivity indices (SI: 1896.5 and 1265.8, respectively). Furthermore, in silico absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) and molecular docking calculations suggested favorable drug-likeness profiles, including improved lipophilicity and non-P-glycoprotein substrate feasibility. The findings validate the molecular hybridization strategy, establishing this new class of compounds as promising, multi-target antiviral prototypes for further preclinical exploration against prevalent viral pathogens.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The research synthesized a novel series of 1,2,3-triazole–quinoline derivatives (compounds 4a–4h) using a molecular hybridization strategy and evaluated their antiviral activity and cytotoxicity in vitro against DENV-2 and other RNA viruses.
analysis.methods: Compounds were synthesized in three steps with moderate-to-high yields, and their inhibitory capacities against DENV-2 and other viruses were assessed in vitro alongside cytotoxicity evaluations across relevant cell lines.
analysis.main_results: Compounds 4a–4h demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral activity, with high inhibition percentages at 10 μM against DENV-2, and compounds 4c and 4e showed exceptional potency and safety against DENV-2, yielding selectivity indices of 1896.5 and 1265.8, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings validate the molecular hybridization strategy, establishing the new class of 1,2,3-triazole–quinoline derivatives as promising multi-target antiviral prototypes for further preclinical exploration against DENV-2 and related pathogens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies potential lead compounds for DENV-2 antiviral development, offering a foundation for future preclinical and translational research to address unmet therapeutic needs in dengue management.

analysis.summary_en: This study synthesized and evaluated a series of 1,2,3-triazole–quinoline derivatives for broad-spectrum antiviral activity, focusing on DENV-2. Compounds 4c and 4e exhibited exceptional potency and safety against DENV-2, with high selectivity indices. The findings support the molecular hybridization strategy and propose these derivatives as promising antiviral prototypes for further preclinical development against DENV-2 and related RNA viruses.

title_zh: 针对 SARS-CoV-2、流感、DENV-2 和 CHIKV 的新型 1,2,3-三唑-喹啉衍生物的合成和广谱 抗病毒药物 评价
source_body_en: The persistent global threat posed by emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, DENV-2, and CHIKV, highlights the critical need for novel and broad-spectrum antiviral agents. Building upon the established antiviral activity of the quinoline scaffold, this study employed a molecular hybridization strategy to design and synthesize a novel series of 1,2,3-triazole–quinoline derivatives (compounds 4a–4h). This approach strategically fused the bioactive quinoline nucleus with the pharmaceutically favorable 1,2,3-triazole ring. The new compounds were synthesized efficiently in three steps with moderate-to-high yields, and their structures were subsequently determined. Their inhibitory capacities against the four viruses and cytotoxicity across relevant cell lines were evaluated in vitro. The initial screening demonstrated that compounds 4a–4h possessed broad-spectrum antiviral activity, showing high inhibition percentages at 10 μM against SARS-CoV-2, DENV-2, and CHIKV. Notably, compounds 4c and 4e, substituted with methoxy and ethyl groups, respectively, displayed exceptional potency and safety against SARS-CoV-2, yielding high selectivity indices (SI: 1896.5 and 1265.8, respectively). Furthermore, in silico absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) and molecular docking calculations suggested favorable drug-likeness profiles, including improved lipophilicity and non-P-glycoprotein substrate feasibility. The findings validate the molecular hybridization strategy, establishing this new class of compounds as promising, multi-target antiviral prototypes for further preclinical exploration against prevalent viral pathogens.

title: Combination of Melittin and Clinacanthus nutans Extract Enhances Antiviral Efficacy Against Dengue Virus Serotype 2 Infection
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a major global health threat, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions, due to the lack of effective antiviral therapies. In this study, we evaluated a novel combination strategy using melittin, a bee venom-derived antiviral peptide, together with Clinacanthus nutans extract to enhance antiviral efficacy while reducing melittin-associated cytotoxicity against dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2). Cytotoxicity was assessed in Vero cells using a cell viability assay, whereas antiviral activity was evaluated by focus-forming unit (FFU) reduction assay, cell-based ELISA, FFU titration assay, and immunofluorescence assay (IFA). Melittin (1.25–2.5 μg/mL) and C. nutans extract (15.625–500 μg/mL) maintained cell viability above 80%, whereas 5 μg/mL melittin markedly reduced cell viability. Notably, co-treatment with C. nutans restored cell viability to above 80%, demonstrating a significant cytoprotective effect. More importantly, the combination treatment exhibited greater antiviral activity than either agent alone, resulting in complete inhibition of viral infection at lower concentrations while simultaneously suppressing intracellular viral protein expression and production of progeny viruses. These findings suggest that C. nutans may enhance the antiviral activity of melittin while reducing its cytotoxicity under the conditions tested. Overall, this study provides preliminary evidence supporting the potential of this natural compound-based combination strategy and warrants further preclinical investigation as a candidate antiviral approach against DENV infection.

The research highlights the need for effective antiviral therapies against DENV, as it remains a significant global health threat. title_zh: 蜂毒肽和 Clinacanthus nutans 提取物的组合增强了 抗病毒药物 对抗 登革病毒 血清型 2 感染的功效
source_body_en: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a major global health threat, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions, due to the lack of effective antiviral therapies. In this study, we evaluated a novel combination strategy using melittin, a bee venom-derived antiviral peptide, together with Clinacanthus nutans extract to enhance antiviral efficacy while reducing melittin-associated cytotoxicity against dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2). Cytotoxicity was assessed in Vero cells using a cell viability assay, whereas antiviral activity was evaluated by focus-forming unit (FFU) reduction assay, cell-based ELISA, FFU titration assay, and immunofluorescence assay (IFA). Melittin (1.25–2.5 μg/mL) and C. nutans extract (15.625–500 μg/mL) maintained cell viability above 80%, whereas 5 μg/mL melittin markedly reduced cell viability. Notably, co-treatment with C. nutans restored cell viability to above 80%, demonstrating a significant cytoprotective effect. More importantly, the combination treatment exhibited greater antiviral activity than either agent alone, resulting in complete inhibition of viral infection at lower concentrations while simultaneously suppressing intracellular viral protein expression and production of progeny viruses. These findings suggest that C. nutans may enhance the antiviral activity of melittin while reducing its cytotoxicity under the conditions tested. Overall, this study provides preliminary evidence supporting the potential of this natural compound-based combination strategy and warrants further preclinical investigation as a candidate antiviral approach against DENV infection.

title: A Study of Liver Dysfunction in Dengue
abstract: Background: Dengue is a major mosquito-borne viral illness associated with a broad spectrum of clinical manifestations ranging from uncomplicated fever to severe dengue with multiorgan involvement. Liver dysfunction is a common laboratory abnormality, but its role in predicting disease severity remains uncertain. Aim: To evaluate liver dysfunction in patients with dengue fever, assess liver function test abnormalities, and determine their association with disease severity, complications, and duration of hospital stay. Materials and Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted between September 2017 and July 2019 at Kasturba Hospital, Manipal. A total of 200 adult patients with serologically confirmed dengue (NS1 antigen or IgM positive) were included. Clinical details and laboratory parameters, including liver function tests, complete blood count, coagulation profile, and renal function tests, were recorded. Patients were categorized into three groups based on AST and ALT elevations and compared with the WHO classification of dengue severity. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS, with a p-value <0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Among the 200 patients, 75% were males, with the highest incidence observed in the 21–30-year age group. Elevated ALT levels were present in 84.5% of patients, while AST elevation was more pronounced than ALT. However, neither AST nor ALT levels showed a statistically significant association with WHO-defined dengue severity (ALT: p=0.600; AST: p=0.224). Hyperbilirubinemia and hypoalbuminemia were uncommon and were not significantly associated with disease severity. Fourteen patients required intensive care, and three deaths were recorded. Liver enzyme elevations did not correlate significantly with hospital stay, ICU requirement, or mortality. Conclusion: Liver dysfunction, particularly elevated AST and ALT levels, is a frequent finding in dengue fever. Although transaminase elevations are common, they do not reliably predict disease severity, hospital stay, ICU admission, or mortality. Liver function tests should therefore be interpreted alongside clinical findings and other laboratory parameters rather than used alone for prognostic assessment. Keywords: Dengue fever; Liver dysfunction; Aspartate aminotransferase (AST); Alanine aminotransferase (ALT).

title: Clinical outcomes of dengue patients requiring intensive care in Brazil: A 10-year nationwide observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue may lead to critical illness requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Even though Brazil is one of the most affected countries worldwide, national data are limited. Understanding clinical severity and outcomes is essential to inform policy and preparedness. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of adult dengue ICU admissions in Brazil from 2015 to 2024 using aggregated data from two nationwide complementary datasets: the Brazilian ICU registry (UTIs Brasileiras) and DATASUS Hospital Information System. The registry dataset includes clinical, severity, and organ-support variables from public and private institutions, while DATASUS captures public-system (SUS) reimbursed hospitalizations. Outcomes were ICU and in-hospital mortality, organ support, and length of stay. RESULTS: We identified 32,016 episodes of dengue admissions in the ICU registry and 11,241 in DATASUS. Data from the registry for the first 24 h of ICU shows mechanical ventilation use in 5.8% and vasopressors use in 7.2%. In-hospital mortality was 8.2% in the ICU registry. In DATASUS, in-hospital mortality was 18.6%. Patients admitted to public hospitals in the ICU registry had unadjusted ICU mortality of 20% and in-hospital mortality of 25%. Unadjusted mortality rates were higher in subgroups like older patients and those in use of vasopressors. CONCLUSION: Dengue requiring ICU admission in Brazil is associated with significant morbimortality. Mortality rates were higher in subgroups such as old patients and those admitted to public hospitals. Further studies are necessary to identify the potentially modifiable, organizational and patient-level factors associated with outcomes.

title_zh: 巴西需要重症监护的登革热患者的临床结果:一项为期 10 年的全国观察性研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Dengue may lead to critical illness requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Even though Brazil is one of the most affected countries worldwide, national data are limited. Understanding clinical severity and outcomes is essential to inform policy and preparedness. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of adult dengue ICU admissions in Brazil from 2015 to 2024 using aggregated data from two nationwide complementary datasets: the Brazilian ICU registry (UTIs Brasileiras) and DATASUS Hospital Information System. The registry dataset includes clinical, severity, and organ-support variables from public and private institutions, while DATASUS captures public-system (SUS) reimbursed hospitalizations. Outcomes were ICU and in-hospital mortality, organ support, and length of stay. RESULTS: We identified 32,016 episodes of dengue admissions in the ICU registry and 11,241 in DATASUS. Data from the registry for the first 24 h of ICU shows mechanical ventilation use in 5.8% and vasopressors use in 7.2%. In-hospital mortality was 8.2% in the ICU registry. In DATASUS, in-hospital mortality was 18.6%. Patients admitted to public hospitals in the ICU registry had unadjusted ICU mortality of 20% and in-hospital mortality of 25%. Unadjusted mortality rates were higher in subgroups like older patients and those in use of vasopressors. CONCLUSION: Dengue requiring ICU admission in Brazil is associated with significant morbimortality. Mortality rates were higher in subgroups such as old patients and those admitted to public hospitals. Further studies are necessary to identify the potentially modifiable, organizational and patient-level factors associated with outcomes.

title: Dengue Fever Complicated by Intracerebral Haemorrhage, Acute Respiratory Failure and Nosocomial Pneumonia: A Case Report
abstract: Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne viral illness caused by the dengue virus. Majority of cases have self-limiting course, rarely severe dengue causes fatal neurological complications like encephalitis and haemorrhage. This is case report of a 38-year-old male who presented with three days of high-grade fever, one day of altered sensorium, headache, and generalised weakness. Serological testing confirmed dengue IgM positivity. The clinical course was complicated by a rapid decline in Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) from 15 to 11, necessitating endotracheal intubation on day two in the setting of blood-stained pulmonary secretions. Highresolution Computed Tomography (CT) of the thorax suggested consolidation with pulmonary oedema. CT of the brain revealed a 3.9×3.8×3.5 cm Intracerebral Parenchymal Haemorrhage (IPH) with surrounding oedema causing significant mass effect. Laboratory parameters documented severe thrombocytopaenia (nadir 0.6 lac/cumm), coagulopathy, hepatocellular injury with peak SGOT/ SGPT of 227/276 IU/L, and elevated C-reactive protein at 85.6 mg/L. Endotracheal aspirate cultures grew extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii on day five, requiring escalation of antimicrobial therapy to meropenem and polymyxin. Supportive management included platelet and Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) transfusion. The patient was successfully extubated on day nine and discharged home on day twelve. Notably, the simultaneous occurrence of dengue-associated Intracerebral Haemorrhage (ICH), acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure, and Multi-Drug Resistant (MDR) nosocomial pneumonia in a young immunocompetent adult represents a triad that is rarely documented in the published literature. Early recognition of neurological deterioration, timely neuroimaging, aggressive blood product support, and targeted antimicrobial therapy with conservative management of ICH remains critical determinants of a favourable outcome.
journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

Majority of cases have self-limiting course, rarely severe dengue causes fatal neurological complications like encephalitis and haemorrhage. This is case report of a 38-year-old male who presented with three days of high-grade fever, one day of altered sensorium, headache, and generalised weakness. Serological testing confirmed dengue IgM positivity. The clinical course was complicated by a rapid decline in Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) from 15 to 11, necessitating endotracheal intubation on day two in the setting of blood-stained pulmonary secretions. Highresolution Computed Tomography (CT) of the thorax suggested consolidation with pulmonary oedema. CT of the brain revealed a 3.9×3.8×3.5 cm Intracerebral Parenchymal Haemorrhage (IPH) with surrounding oedema causing significant mass effect. Laboratory parameters documented severe thrombocytopaenia (nadir 0.6 lac/cumm), coagulopathy, hepatocellular injury with peak SGOT/ SGPT of 227/276 IU/L, and elevated C-reactive protein at 85.6 mg/L. Endotracheal aspirate cultures grew extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii on day five, requiring escalation of antimicrobial therapy to meropenem and polymyxin. Supportive management included platelet and Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) transfusion. The patient was successfully extubated on day nine and discharged home on day twelve. Notably, the simultaneous occurrence of dengue-associated Intracerebral Haemorrhage (ICH), acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure, and Multi-Drug Resistant (MDR) nosocomial pneumonia in a young immunocompetent adult represents a triad that is rarely documented in the published literature. Early recognition of neurological deterioration, timely neuroimaging, aggressive blood product support, and targeted antimicrobial therapy with conservative management of ICH remains critical determinants of a favourable outcome.
source_records.journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
